2pl_latent_reg_irt: Australian and Japanese students in the First International Mathematics Study, from the TAM package. A two-parameter IRT model with a latent regression: person ability is itself regressed on covariates, and the last item difficulty is fixed by the sum-to-zero constraint on the rest.
GLMM1_model: Simulated peregrine falcon counts across sites in the French Jura over nine years, from the Bayesian Population Analysis book. A Poisson GLMM with a random site effect and nothing else, and the counts at the unobserved site-years imputed in generated quantities.
GLMM_Poisson_model: Simulated peregrine counts with a random year effect, from the Bayesian Population Analysis book. A cubic time trend on the log rate plus one normal effect per year, so the trend and the noise around it are fit together.
GLM_Binomial_model: Broods and successful broods of peregrines in the French Jura, 1964 to 2003. Binomial logistic regression of nesting success on a quadratic in year, three parameters and flat priors.
GLM_Poisson_model: The peregrine population breeding in the French Jura, 1964 to 2003. Poisson regression of the count on a cubic in year, with implicit uniform priors, which is about as small as a real model gets.
M0_model: Simulated capture-recapture histories under a constant detection probability, from the Bayesian Population Analysis book. Data augmentation with the latent presence indicator summed out by hand, so the likelihood is a log_sum_exp per never-detected individual and population size is drawn in generated quantities.
Mb_model: Simulated capture-recapture data where being caught changes the probability of being caught again. Same augmented likelihood as M0, but detection on each occasion depends on whether the individual was caught on the previous one, which is the trap-response term reported at the end.
Mh_model: Aggregated capture frequencies, one count per individual. Detection varies by individual through a logit-normal random effect, which is what turns a three-parameter model into 388 parameters.
Mt_model: Simulated capture histories over three occasions. Detection varies by occasion rather than by individual, so there is one probability per sampling occasion and the augmented likelihood is the same shape as M0.
Mtbh_model: Wryneck counts from five-minute point counts every 500 m along a transect crossing Czechia, repeated five times in one breeding season. The full model: detection varies by occasion, by individual, and with whether the bird was detected last time, all three at once.
Mth_model: Simulated capture histories over five occasions, unaggregated. Detection varies by occasion and by individual together, the two effects added on the logit scale.
Rate_1_model: Five correct answers out of ten questions. One parameter, a beta prior, a binomial likelihood, and the whole posterior is conjugate and known in closed form, which makes it a good first thing to run.
Rate_2_model: Successes from two trials of different sizes. One rate per trial and their difference as a transformed parameter, from the Bayesian Cognitive Modeling book.
Rate_3_model: The same two trials, but now assuming a single shared rate, so both counts inform one parameter.
Rate_4_model: One trial of fifteen, with a second rate that no data touches. Sampling the untouched parameter is how the prior predictive gets drawn alongside the posterior predictive in generated quantities.
Rate_5_model: Two trials, one with no successes and one with nothing but successes, sharing a rate. The disagreement between the two is the point, and it shows up in the posterior predictive counts.
Survey_model: Returned surveys from an unknown number sent. The number sent is discrete, which Stan cannot sample, so the model builds the log probability for every possible value and marginalizes with log_sum_exp, then recovers the discrete posterior with softmax in generated quantities.
accel_gp: The MASS motorcycle acceleration data, run through brms. Two approximate Gaussian processes with a basis-function expansion, one for the mean and one for the log residual scale, so the noise level is allowed to change over time.
accel_splines: The same motorcycle crash data, fit with penalized splines instead of Gaussian processes. Thirty-eight basis functions for the mean and thirty-eight for the log scale, with the spline coefficients given a non-centered scale parameter.
arK: Simulated data from an order-five autoregression. The likelihood is a scalar loop over time steps with the lag terms accumulated by hand, which is a shape stanli rewrites into vectorized ops.
arma11: Simulated ARMA(1,1) data. Each prediction error depends on the previous one, so the recursion cannot be vectorized on either side and both engines end up doing scalar work.
blr: A hundred simulated observations with five coefficients, built so the coefficients correlate at 0.8 in the posterior. Plain linear regression, present as a well-understood shape for samplers to be tested on.
bones_model: Thirty-four indicators of skeletal maturity read from radiographs of thirteen boys aged six months to eighteen years. A graded-response model over items with two to five ordered categories, with the category probabilities built from differences of cumulative logits and missing grades skipped.
bym2_offset_only: Reported traffic accidents involving a pedestrian or cyclist in New York City, aggregated to 1921 census tracts. The BYM2 spatial model: a Poisson rate per tract split between unstructured heterogeneity and a spatially structured effect over the adjacency graph, with the split controlled by one mixing parameter.
covid19imperial_v2: ECDC covid-19 death counts for fourteen countries up to 2020-04-01, with the dates of government interventions. The Imperial College report 13 model: infections are seeded, convolved forward with a serial interval, and mapped to deaths through an infection-fatality delay, with the reproduction number reduced multiplicatively by each intervention.
covid19imperial_v3: The same ECDC death counts and the next revision of the Imperial College model. The forward simulation is identical to v2 here, and posteriordb keeps both so the two can be compared on the same data.
diamonds: Five thousand diamonds from the ggplot2 dataset, prepared by brms. Linear regression on 24 centered predictors through normal_id_glm, which is one fused op for the whole likelihood, and the largest dataset the page will load.
dogs: Thirty dogs learning to avoid a shock over twenty-five trials, from the Gelman and Hill book. Log odds of avoidance are linear in the number of previous shocks and previous avoidances, both accumulated in transformed parameters.
dogs_hierarchical: The same avoidance-learning experiment, written with the probability as a product of two learning rates raised to the counts. Two parameters, both on the unit interval, and the posterior predictive replayed trial by trial.
dogs_log: The avoidance-learning data again, with the linear predictor on the log scale and no intercept, so the coefficients are constrained to opposite signs by their uniform priors.
dogs_nonhierarchical: The learning-rate parameterization given one pair of rates per dog, drawn from a shared distribution with an LKJ prior on their correlation. Despite the name, this is the hierarchical version of the pair.
dugongs_model: Ages and lengths of twenty-seven captured dugongs, a classic from the BUGS examples. A nonlinear growth curve where length approaches an asymptote geometrically, so the rate parameter appears in an exponent rather than a product.
earn_height: Heights and earnings from a national survey, from the Gelman and Hill book. Earnings regressed on height in dollars, unlogged, which is chapter four's illustration of a fit whose residuals are obviously wrong.
eight_schools_centered: The SAT coaching study from Rubin (1981), eight schools with an estimated effect and a standard error each. The centered parameterization, whose funnel-shaped posterior is the standard demonstration of what a sampler struggles with when the group scale can approach zero.
eight_schools_noncentered: The same eight schools, reparameterized so the school effects are standard normal and scaled afterwards. The funnel goes away, which is why this is the version people are told to write.
election88_full: Seven CBS News polls from the week before the 1988 presidential election. Multilevel logistic regression with varying intercepts by age, education, their interaction, state, and region, which is the worked example behind poststratification.
garch11: Simulated GARCH(1,1) data. The conditional variance at each step is built from the previous step's variance, so the whole likelihood is a serial recursion that nothing can vectorize.
gp_pois_regr: Simulated counts from a Poisson process with a Gaussian process log rate. The covariance is built, Cholesky factored, and applied to standard normal draws every leapfrog step, so the cost is cubic in the number of points.
gp_regr: The same simulated points with a Gaussian likelihood instead of Poisson. Three hyperparameters, and the latent function integrated out analytically through multi_normal_cholesky rather than sampled.
gpcm_latent_reg_irt: TIMSS 2011 mathematics responses from 500 Australian and Taiwanese students. A generalized partial credit model: each ordered response category gets its own step parameter, and person ability is regressed on covariates.
grsm_latent_reg_irt: Attitudes to science from the 1992 Euro-Barometer survey in Great Britain. A generalized rating scale model, which is the partial credit model with the step structure shared across items instead of estimated per item.
hier_2pl: Grade 12 science assessment responses from Wood et al. (2003). A two-parameter IRT model where item discrimination and difficulty are drawn together from a bivariate normal, with an LKJ prior on the correlation between them.
hierarchical_gp: State-level presidential vote shares over time. Gaussian processes over years at both the region and the state level, each a sum of a long and a short length scale, with the total variance split across seventeen components by a Dirichlet.
hmm_drive_0: SportVU player tracking from an NBA game, reduced to inverse speed and distance to the hoop. A two-state hidden Markov model with exponential emissions, the forward algorithm written out by hand, and Viterbi decoding in generated quantities. The forward pass is a recurrence, which is the shape stanli is slowest on.
hmm_drive_1: The same tracking data with normal emissions instead of exponential, and the emission scales supplied as data. Same hand-written forward algorithm and the same serial dependence through time.
hmm_example: A short simulated series with two states and one observed output. The smallest hidden Markov model here, and the clearest read of the forward algorithm.
hmm_gaussian: Simulated data for a Gaussian hidden Markov model. The forward pass lives in transformed parameters, so the whole filtered state matrix is carried along, and generated quantities adds the backward pass, the smoothed states, and Viterbi.
iohmm_reg: Simulated data for an input-output hidden Markov model. Both the transition probabilities and the emission means depend on a covariate at each time step, so the transition matrix is rebuilt from a softmax at every step of the recurrence.
irt_2pl: Simulated responses from a two-parameter IRT model. Discrimination is lognormal and difficulty normal, both with estimated scales, and the likelihood is one vectorized bernoulli_logit per item.
kidscore_interaction: Cognitive test scores of three- and four-year-olds against their mothers' education and IQ. Linear regression with the interaction between the two predictors formed in transformed data.
kidscore_interaction_c: The same test scores with both predictors centered at their means before the interaction is formed, which is chapter four's point about what an intercept means.
kidscore_interaction_c2: The same model centered on interpretable reference points instead of the sample means: an IQ of 100 and half of a high school diploma.
kidscore_interaction_z: The same model again with both predictors standardized by two standard deviations, so the coefficients are comparable to each other.
kidscore_mom_work: The same children, regressed instead on whether and when the mother returned to work, expanded into three indicator variables against a baseline.
kidscore_momhs: Test scores against a single binary predictor, whether the mother finished high school. Two coefficients and a scale.
kidscore_momhsiq: Test scores against both mother's high school completion and IQ, with no interaction between them.
kidscore_momiq: Test scores against mother's IQ alone, the simplest fit in the series.
kilpisjarvi: Mean summer temperature at Kilpisjarvi in Finnish Lapland, 1952 to 2013, with the years left unshifted. Linear regression whose slope and intercept are strongly correlated in the posterior precisely because the predictor is not centered.
ldaK2: A simulated corpus of three documents and 1200 tokens generated from three topics, fit with only two. Latent Dirichlet allocation with the topic assignments marginalized out, and a posterior that is multimodal by construction because the third topic has nowhere to go.
ldaK5: Pride and Prejudice, tokenized by chapter with stop words and rare words removed, fit with five topics. Every token contributes a log_sum_exp over topics, and the per-topic word distributions are what make this 7714 parameters.
log10earn_height: Earnings against height with the response on a log base ten scale, so coefficients read as changes per order of magnitude.
logearn_height: Earnings against height with a natural log response, the fix for the untransformed version in the same series.
logearn_height_male: Log earnings against height and sex, without an interaction, so the sex term is a constant vertical shift.
logearn_interaction: Log earnings against height, sex, and their interaction, which lets the height slope differ between men and women.
logearn_interaction_z: The same interaction model with height standardized first, which is what makes the main effects interpretable when an interaction is present.
logearn_logheight_male: Log earnings against log height and sex, so the height coefficient is an elasticity rather than dollars per inch.
logistic_regression_rhs: An ovarian cancer microarray: 1536 gene expression predictors and 54 patients. Logistic regression with the regularized horseshoe prior, whose local scales are shrunk toward zero and then capped by a slab, which is how a model with more predictors than patients stays identified.
logmesquite: Mesquite bushes weighed after harvest against measurements taken before it. Every predictor and the response logged, seven coefficients, from chapter four's model-building sequence.
logmesquite_logva: The same bushes with the individual dimensions replaced by canopy volume and canopy area, which is the transformation that makes the fit interpretable.
logmesquite_logvas: Volume, area and shape together with total height, density and group, the widest of the mesquite variants.
logmesquite_logvash: Volume, area, shape and total height, dropping the density term.
logmesquite_logvolume: Leaf weight against canopy volume alone, two coefficients, the end of the simplification.
losscurve_sislob: Insurance loss development by underwriting cohort. Cumulative losses follow a growth curve in time, either Weibull or log-logistic depending on a data flag, scaled by a per-cohort loss ratio drawn from a shared lognormal.
lotka_volterra: Hudson Bay lynx and hare pelt counts, 1900 to 1920. A predator-prey ODE solved with rk45 inside the model, and the posterior predictive drawn in generated quantities. ODE models are the shape stanli is slowest on.
low_dim_gauss_mix: Simulated draws from two well-separated Gaussians. A two-component mixture with the means ordered to break label switching, and log_mix evaluated per observation.
low_dim_gauss_mix_collapse: The same mixture fit to poorly separated data, and with the ordering constraint removed. The posterior collapses into a bowtie where the two components can swap, which is the geometry the model is here to demonstrate.
lsat_model: Response patterns from a five-item Law School Aptitude Test, expanded from cumulative frequencies back to a thousand students. A one-parameter IRT model, so it carries one ability per student and five item difficulties.
mesquite: The mesquite bushes with no transformations at all, weight regressed directly on the raw measurements. The starting point that the logged variants improve on.
multi_occupancy: Butterfly species observed across grazed grasslands in south-central Sweden in July 1997. A multi-species occupancy model: occupancy and detection are correlated species-level effects, the community is augmented with species that were never seen, and their presence is summed out.
nes: The 1972 National Election Study. Party identification regressed on ideology, ethnicity, age bracket, education, sex and income, with the age brackets expanded into indicators.
nes_logit_model: The 1992 National Election Study, reduced to a Bush or Clinton preference against family income. Logistic regression with two parameters, written through bernoulli_logit_glm.
nn_rbm1bJ10: The first hundred MNIST train and test digits. A one-hidden-layer neural network with ten hidden units and a categorical output, sampled rather than optimized, with the weight scales given inverse gamma priors. Nearly eight thousand parameters and a posterior with as many symmetries as there are ways to permute the hidden units.
normal_mixture: Draws from a bimodal Gaussian with known unit variance. Two means and one mixing weight, and no ordering constraint, so the two labels are exchangeable.
normal_mixture_k: Draws from five Gaussians with unknown means, scales and weights. Every observation costs a log_sum_exp over all five components, and the label symmetry is five-way.
one_comp_mm_elim_abs: A pharmacokinetic experiment: one dose, one compartment, concentrations measured over time. Absorption is first order and elimination is Michaelis-Menten, solved with the stiff bdf integrator rather than rk45.
pilots: Success rates of pilots on a flight simulator, five treatments crossed with eight airports. Varying intercepts for both factors with no interaction, the smallest crossed random effects model in the corpus.
prophet: Daily rstan download counts from CRAN, prepared for Facebook's prophet model. A piecewise linear trend with twenty-five changepoints under a Laplace prior, plus Fourier seasonality terms that enter either additively or multiplicatively.
radon_county: Radon measurements from homes across counties in the United States, in the modified form used by the warmup paper. Intercept per county drawn from a shared normal and nothing else, the plainest hierarchical model in the radon series.
radon_county_intercept: Radon measurements from 12573 homes across 386 counties. A separate unpooled intercept per county plus one shared floor coefficient, which is the no-pooling end of the radon case study.
radon_hierarchical_intercept_centered: The full radon model: county intercepts drawn from a shared normal, with county uranium as a group-level predictor and floor as a house-level one. The centered parameterization, where the intercepts are sampled directly.
radon_hierarchical_intercept_noncentered: The same full radon model with the county intercepts written as standard normal draws scaled by the group scale. The reparameterization that keeps the sampler out of the funnel when the group scale is small.
radon_partially_pooled_centered: Radon with county intercepts and no predictors at all, sampled directly. The partial pooling baseline the rest of the series builds on.
radon_partially_pooled_noncentered: The same intercepts-only model reparameterized away from the funnel.
radon_pooled: Radon with one intercept and one floor coefficient for the whole country, ignoring counties entirely. Three parameters over 12573 observations, and the complete pooling end of the case study.
radon_variable_intercept_centered: Radon with a county intercept and a single shared floor slope, sampled in the centered parameterization.
radon_variable_intercept_noncentered: The varying intercept model with the intercepts scaled from standard normals instead.
radon_variable_intercept_slope_centered: Radon with both the intercept and the floor slope varying by county, each drawn from its own shared normal. Two parameters per county, which doubles the model to 777.
radon_variable_intercept_slope_noncenter: The varying intercept and slope model with both sets of county effects reparameterized away from their funnels.
radon_variable_slope_centered: Radon with one shared intercept but a floor slope that varies by county, sampled directly.
radon_variable_slope_noncentered: The varying slope model with the county slopes scaled from standard normals.
rats_model: Weights of thirty young rats measured weekly for five weeks, from the BUGS examples. A growth curve with an intercept and slope per rat, both drawn from shared normals, with age centered so the two are not correlated.
seeds_centered_model: Germination counts by seed type and root extract, from Crowder (1978). Binomial logistic regression with a random effect per plate, recentered to sum to zero, and priors tightened from the original BUGS version.
seeds_model: The same germination data with the original BUGS priors: normal with a standard deviation of a thousand, and a gamma on the precision with both parameters at 1e-3. Worth running next to the other two to see what those priors do.
seeds_stanified_model: The same model with the vague priors replaced by weakly informative ones and the precision parameterization dropped in favor of a scale.
sesame_one_pred_a: An experiment where parents were randomly encouraged to have their children watch Sesame Street. The first stage of an instrumental variables analysis: whether the child watched, regressed on the encouragement.
soil_incubation: Twenty-five measurements of evolved carbon dioxide from a soil incubation experiment. Carbon moves between two pools, each decomposing at its own rate and feeding the other, solved as an ODE and compared against the cumulative measurements.
state_space_stochastic_level_stochastic_: Monthly UK road casualty counts, from the state space time series text. Both the level and the twelve-month seasonal pattern follow random walks, which makes the model one long chain of dependencies with 389 parameters.
surgical_model: Cardiac surgery mortality in twelve hospitals operating on infants. A binomial model with per-hospital log odds drawn from a shared normal, which is the canonical demonstration of shrinking a small hospital's rate toward the population mean.
wells_daae_c_model: Households in Bangladesh deciding whether to switch away from an arsenic-contaminated well. Distance, arsenic level, their interaction, membership of a community association and years of education, with the continuous predictors centered.
wells_dae_c_model: The switching decision on centered distance, arsenic, their interaction, and education.
wells_dae_inter_model: The switching decision with all three predictors centered and all three pairwise interactions included.
wells_dae_model: The switching decision on distance, arsenic and education, rescaled but not centered, with no interactions.
wells_dist: The switching decision on distance alone, written as a plain bernoulli_logit rather than through the GLM form. Two parameters.
wells_dist100_model: Distance alone again, rescaled to hundreds of metres and routed through bernoulli_logit_glm, which is one fused op for the whole likelihood.
wells_dist100ars_model: The switching decision on rescaled distance and arsenic level, three parameters.
wells_interaction_c_model: Distance and arsenic centered, with their interaction, so the main effects are read at the average household.
wells_interaction_model: Distance and arsenic uncentered, with their interaction, which is the version whose coefficients are easy to misread.
